First couple of days went well, then I had a family emergency that took me across the US for 4 days. This put me in a position where I'm in a city I've never been to, with a very sick family member that I'd only visit for about an hour at a time (not a close family member, but my only opportunity to say goodbye) and left me to my own devices for nearly the entire time I was there, save for a few stints with my family (that I'm not close to, at all). This ended up being two entire days inside airports and airplanes (to and from), and two entire days in a place I've never been before with a whole lot of time on my hands.

**I wish I could say that I didn't drink alcohol. I did.**

**I wish I could say I didn't eat every meal out for 4 days straight. I did.**

I was mostly alone in a town I'd never been to and I do enjoy seeing things and sight-seeing. One of the things I like to do when in a new place is to find Irish pubs, usually good conversation and learn about some local things to do... also get a feel for the place. While I need to get my alcohol issues under control, I don't think this behavior is really the problem. Sitting on the couch nightly with a bottle of whiskey is the problem behavior. So I kind of took the week off.

Thursday was an air travel day; knowing the food associated with it I chose to basically fast during my trip there. I ate a berry parfait (250 kcal) and nothing else the rest of the travel day. I arrived that night and did go to an establishment for dinner and beer. **I was able to keep under my calorie limit for the day.**

Friday I ate a whole lot of southern food, went to an Irish pub in the evening, and was **way over budget**.

Saturday I had an agenda so I did some sight seeing, skipped breakfast and had a late lunch / early dinner. I only ate about half of it, so **I was at below 1000 calories for the day**.

Sunday was another air travel day; I had my morning berry parfait and stayed there until my last flight. It got delayed 5 hours so I went out and had dinner and a couple of beers to pass the time, kind of finish off my bad week. **It was budgeted for, so it ended up okay.**

While I did not make my goal of not drinking, I did keep it under control and budgeted. I only went over the one day so I was able to do enough to have lost about 0.6lbs, better than last week. **All things considered, knowing I needed to keep everything closely budgeted kept me on track.**

This coming week will be back to what I've planned, so an early hiccup but still in reasonable shape.
Week 2. Not great. CW 300.2, down 0.6lbs this week, down 2.7lbs total.

Sometimes life kicks you in the nuts. Sorry to hear about your family member.

At least you didn't gain weight for the week, considering you were gone for over half of it, that's not bad. Only thing to do now is double down on routine and diet and start back up again.

Yes, it was definitely bad timing. I came out okay, but definitely not how I'd have wanted to. The good news is that I'm probably a bit bloated due to sodium and alcohol and it'll fall off this week. Next week will be under 300, never to return.
